{% raw %}
`wget`: download a file from the internet.

## Synopsis

<strong>wget</strong> \[<strong>-q</strong>\] \[<strong>-O</strong> <em>file</em>\] <em>url</em>

## Description

<strong>wget</strong> downloads what <em>url</em> names, through the computer's internet card, following redirects, into a file named as the URL's last part (<strong>index.html</strong> when it has none). A URL without a scheme is <strong>http://</strong>'s. It says what it does on standard error.

The card reaches only the public internet: never the server's own machine or network (the server's settings may allow more, or less).

## Options

<strong>-q</strong>
: Says nothing.

<strong>-O</strong> <em>file</em>
: Saves to <em>file</em> instead (<strong>-</strong>: standard output).

## Exit status

0 when it saved the file; 2 for bad usage; 3 when the file can't be written; 4 for a network failure (refused, an unknown host, timed out); 8 when the server answered with an error (4xx, 5xx).

## Examples

```text
wget https://example.com/
wget -O notes.txt https://example.com/notes
```

## Notes

GNU <strong>wget</strong>'s recursion, retries and resuming (<strong>-r</strong>, <strong>-t</strong>, <strong>-c</strong>) are not supported.

## See also

<strong>curl</strong>(1)
